THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Queensland Natural Resources Minister Howard Hobbs yesterday defended his State's decision to call a halt to development of leasehold land in the State following the High Court's Wik decision. Hobbs said that as a result of legal advice the State "had no alternative" and he dismissed claims the Government had mounted a scaremongering campaign on the Wik issue. Page 3.

The Department of Foreign Affairs says French President Jacques Chirac warmly praised Australia's rescues of stranded British and French yachtsmen by singling out Australian ambassador to France, John Spencer, at a New Year's reception at the diplomatic corps at the Elysee Palace in Paris. Page 3.

Finance Minister John Fahey and Acting Industry Minister Peter McGauran yesterday moved to quell fears from car manufacturers over further tariff cuts after the Ford Motor Company said it may have to close down its Australian operations if the recommendaton of the Productivity Commission to reduced tariffs by five per cent was taken up. Page 4.

Australian Bureau of Statistics figures showed yesterday there was a strong increase in private sector job vacancies during the three months to November, figures that show a rebound in Australia's labour market. Vacancies rose 1.7 per cent to be 9.3 per cent higher than a year earlier in seasonally adjusted terms. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Solo yachtsman Tony Bullimore has told how he survived four days and nights in the hull of his capsized yacht in freezing Southern Ocean conditions. In a dramatic rescue, described by Bullimore as one of the "greatest search-and-rescue efforts", HMAS Adelide rescued the Englishman and Frenchman Thierry Dubois after steaming from Perth for three days half-way to Antarctica. In a four metre swell and 40-knot winds, Royal Australian Navy engineers made their way from HMAS Adelaide to the stricken vessel in a rubber inflatable and Bullimore managed to swim to the surface in an effort which was described by one Maritime Safety Authority spokesperson as an "absolute Houdini act". Page 1.

The Federal Government moved quickly to calm car industry concerns over tariff cuts following a controversial Productivity Commission draft recommendation to slash protection levels. Cabinet assured the industry it was not "locked in" to accepting recommedations after Ford's US chief executive, Sir Alexander Trotman, threatened to shut down Ford production in Australia if tariffs were cut below 15 per cent. Page 2.

Job seekers have been given renewed hope as Australian Bureau of Statistics figures reveal job vacancies are back to the strong levels of early last year. Private sector vacancies rose by 8.7 per cent and public sector vacancies by 3.1 per cent between Auust and November last year. Total job vacancies increased by 7.9 per cent during the December quarter, compared with increases of 2 per cent and 5 per cent in preceding quarters. Page 2.
New South Wales Opposition Leader Michael Collins has warned Prime Minister John Howard to show leadership on the republican issue.

Collins has challenged Howard to announce on Australia Day whether the Coalition will proceed with its election promise to hold a people's convention, failing to do so, the Opposition Leader claims the Federal Government risks eroding voter support. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

International praise for the heroic efforts of the Royal Australian Navy came flowing in yesterday following the dramatic rescue of shipwrecked yachtsmen Englishman Tony Bullimore and Frenchman Thierry Dubois from deep in the Southern Ocean. Dubois was airlifted to HMAS Adelaide which was situated 30 kilometres by the side of Bullimore's capsized vessel. The 58-year-old swam out of the hull of his yacht where he had huddled for over 89 hours and boarded an inflatable navy vessel. Page 1.

Janet Holmes a Court's Heytesbury Pastoral Company has come under fire from maritime unions for contracting services from an ageing Singapore-registered ship which is paying a Third World crew the lowest wages ever recorded on a livestock ship in Australin ports.
The crew is being paid at least A$498 under International Labour Organisation monthly wage rates. Page 1.

The Federal Opposition yesterday reaffirmed its commitment to immigration saying it could raise current levels to meet a population target for 50 years hence. In an attempt to steer the current immigration debate from what Opposition Immigration spokesperon Duncan Kerr labelled as "short-term" and "knee-jerk", Labor claimed it would set levels in the context of a sustainable population target. Page 3.

New South Wales Police yesterday released a computer photo-image of a man who has robbed and raped nine women in northern Sydney suburbs over the past 18 months. However, Police are unsure if the attacks have been made by the same man as the victims had gven varying descriptions of the offender. Page 3.
THE AGE

After his dramatic rescue in the Southern Ocean, British yachtsman Tony Bullimore said the 'bang bang bang' of HMAS Adelaide was like heaven. The ship's crew were celebrating, as Bullimore's rescue was the second of the day, with Frenchman Thierry Dubois saved four hours earlier in the same region. Page A1.

Police spokesman James Tonkin said last night the offices of the Victoria Police drug squad were raided yesterday by internal affairs following a burglary at the St Kilda Road headquarters last weekend and concerns over missing files. Files relating to a five-year drug investigation had disappeared, and the force's new anti-corruption body, the ethical standards department and the crime department were conducting an internal investigation. Page A1.

The rescue of round-the-world yachtsmen Thierry Dubois and Tony Bullimore by Australia's defence forces and sea-rescue authorities has been praised by Vendee Globe Challenge yacht race director Phillipe Jeantot, who said that people all over the world have admired the way the Australian Navy conducted the rescue. Page A1. --

While the Howard Government has tried to cut the intake of immigration amid high unemployment concerns, the Federal Opposition's immigration spokesman Duncan Kerr has signalled the Labor Party's support for increased immigration in the longer term to halt the ageing and decline of Australia's population. Page A3. -- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
